content:
sam: Heads-up — ran into repeat OOMs on canary serving cluster while exercising kv-cache heavy traffic. rate ~250 r/s, avg seq ~1024. Allocator trace + nvprof attached below (snip).

nisha: Ugh. Did this correlate with the kernel-routing change last week or a model update?

sam: No model change. Seen on commit a1b2c3. Memory shows a sawtooth: steady growth during many concurrent sessions, then a large cudamalloc failure when a workspace allocation of ~120MB was requested. Example log: 

```
2026-03-17T22:40:12Z INFO allocator: reserve request id=0xabc size=125829120
2026-03-17T22:40:12Z ERROR allocator: cudamalloc failed: out of memory (alloc=125829120, free_total=84213760)
2026-03-17T22:40:12Z WARN runtime: falling back to spill or fail
```

sam: KV cache entries are long-lived (~2000 tokens) so we see many pinned buffers. Suspect fragmentation + split behavior in the PyTorch/CUDA allocator knobs.

ben: What are current knob settings on canary?

sam: Current (observed via /debug/knobs):
```
expandable_segments: false
max_split_size_mb: 128
garbage_collection_threshold: 0.5
```

ben: Two quick ideas: 1) try enabling `expandable_segments` to let the allocator merge small free chunks instead of forcing large contiguous allocations; 2) lower `max_split_size_mb` so we avoid large split allocations that can blow up when caches fragment.

maya: FYI when we enabled expandable segments in a different workload it reduced transient OOMs but slightly increased tail latency due to extra bookkeeping. Worth A/B.

sam: Agreed. Also suspect garbage collection threshold maybe too low — we should force earlier GC to compact before large workspaces are requested.

ben: Proposed configs to test:
```
# A: fragmentation-first
expandable_segments: true
max_split_size_mb: 64
garbage_collection_threshold: 0.7

# B: conservative splits
expandable_segments: false
max_split_size_mb: 32
garbage_collection_threshold: 0.8
```

nisha: Can we capture per-kernel peak memory and allocator histograms for both runs? Need to check if certain kernels (e.g., fused-attn) are amplifying working set.

infra-bot: Deployed canary runs: cluster canary-7 (config A) and canary-8 (config B). Logs will be at http://infra/logs/canary-7 and /canary-8.

maya: I'll run a 3h steady-state replay and record nvprof as well as runtime allocator event traces.

devex-bot: Added a short checklist for this experiment: https://confluence.internal/redwood/eng-runtime/kv-warmup-oom-playbook (steps, expected metrics, traces).

sam: Early numbers after 30m:
- baseline (old knobs): p95 memory peak 94GB, p99 OOM rate ~0.6%
- config A: p95 peak 88GB, p99 OOM 0.02%
- config B: p95 peak 91GB, p99 OOM 0.1%
Latency change (p50/p95) negligible for A, +3% p95 for B.

ben: Sounds like A (expandable_segments + bigger GC threshold) is winning for this workload. Fragmentation suppressed and fewer large failed allocations.

nisha: Interesting. Any change in KV cache hit/warmup timings? We may be evicting too aggressively with a higher GC threshold.

maya: Warmup delays are +10-20ms per session for A. Nothing critical for product path. I'll attach the allocator histogram output: shows many small free chunks in the 8-32MB range pre-A and they get consolidated post-A.

sam: Plan: roll A to 10% for next 24h, capture full-day traces, and if stable, 100% next week. Also add a metric: failed_workspace_alloc_count to alert earlier.

ben: Also worth testing a hybrid knob: enable expandable_segments but keep max_split_size_mb at 96 to see if we get best of both.

nisha: Good call. I'll add that as config C in rollout plan.

devex-bot: Noted — added config C to the checklist.

sam: Thanks all. If anyone hits regressions in perf dashboards, tag me and @nisha. We'll revert quickly if we see adverse impact. :thumbsup:
